sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +6.2 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved +114 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 5.3 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 7.7 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.

Payout Ratio Sustainability: Dividends absorbed 71% of earnings against free cash flow of 234% of net profit. The payout is above what the business generates, so it depends on cash reserves or borrowing.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 25.7% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 226 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 2 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 21 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded 5.8% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 3 hard red flags and 5 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 65/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
